**Triage: `pm:queue` + `pm:blocked` + `domain:devx`.** No `target:<major>`.

## Classification

Queue, not `finding`. Doc-drift cards are usually observation-class, but this one is graded on what the ledger *is*: `validate-null-guards.ts`'s module-header table is the artefact the next author reads to decide whether a seam gets the gate — it is a decision input, and #4811 exists precisely because "a surface excluded without a reason and a surface nobody ever looked at are indistinguishable". A ledger whose evidence column points at code that no longer exists is worse than an absent row, as the body says. The fix is mechanical, its landing site is a named file and a named table row, and its acceptance is checkable by inspection.

The body's two halves are correctly separated and only half 1 is in scope for this card:

1. **Ledger correction** — rewrite the binding/evidence columns to the shape after #6454; keep `verdict: excluded` but swap the reason from "the binding is sparse, so the rule would prescribe the wrong fix" to "ruling clause 3 requires both server-side seams before the gate widens". Small, mechanical.
2. **Gate widening** — clause 3 of the #4953 ruling, prerequisite not met (the flow trigger-record seeding half is unfiled). Not this card's work; when it happens, the fail-policy asymmetry the body identifies (validation rules and hook conditions fail **closed**, `readonlyWhen` fails **open** except #4889's unbound root) must go into the evidence column.

`pm:blocked` per the body's `Blocked-by:` lines. Both stand as written: **PR #6454 is open and still draft** (verified), and the services half of clause 1 (flow trigger-record seeding) has no issue yet. Correcting the ledger before #6454 merges would simply make it lie in the other direction, so the block is real ordering, not caution.

## Routing rationale (landing site, not title vocabulary)

`domain:devx`. The fix lands in `packages/lint/src/validate-null-guards.ts` (module header), and `packages/lint` ⇒ `domain:devx` per the skill's domain table. The title's `readonlyWhen` vocabulary points at engine semantics — this is exactly the case the anchoring rule warns about (#4775): the topic is engine, the *file* is lint.

The `packages/objectql/src/cel-fault.ts` module-header line the body offers as a rider ("in front of **both** evaluators" becomes three after #6454) sits in `domain:engine-core` territory. It is one sentence of drift with the same cause, so it is left folded into this card rather than split — but the implementing seat should note that touching it crosses a lane boundary, and if the two-line edit turns into anything more it belongs in a separate `domain:engine-core` card, not in this one.

## Stale-premise check

`git log --oneline -10 origin/main -- packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` shows `9bc846b` (#4977 / #6440, `requiredWhen` parent binding) landed two hours ago — same family, different seam, and it does not disturb the row this card is about. The ledger row quoted in the body is still verbatim on main; PR #6454 has not merged, so the ledger is still telling the truth *right now* — this card is armed for the moment it stops.

## Release board

Not `target:v17`. Internal tooling documentation; nothing on a shipped surface, no user-visible behaviour, and the gate widening it unblocks is itself a ruling-gated follow-up rather than a release obligation.

## Dedup

Full-text scan of all 455 open issues and PRs across the three repos. No duplicate. Adjacent by shared origin, distinct in landing site: **#6457** (the other spin-off from PR #6454 — the `parent` root's sparse header binding, lands in `packages/objectql`), **PR #6454** itself, **#4953** (the ruling). The body's own note that #4811 is closed and so this is not filed as its sub-issue is correct and needs no correction.

本评论来自分诊座位 Routine(#5474 试点),不构成认领。

⚠️ **The correction is not a one-word swap, and this is the part worth getting right.** #6454's own measurement grid shows the change is not uniformly "now materialized": one cell **flipped in the opposite direction**. `!has(record.<declared>)` went from `true → strips` to `false → passes` — a lock spelled that way *stopped* locking. A ledger row that now reads "materialized" without recording that reversal would be a second false statement replacing the first. Read #6454's grid and the contract note in `packages/objectql/src/declared-fields.ts`, and make the row say what is actually true.

Also check the neighbouring rows while you are in the file: #6454 says two server-side seams were required and it delivered one share. If another row is stale for the same reason, fix it in the same pass and say so; if it is *not* stale, say that too. ⛔ Do not widen the lint gate itself — that is #4811 and ruling item 3, and it waits for both seams.
